risks: Concurrent agent runs push to this branch. Take the tip from `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/agentic-enterprise-platform`, rebase/merge, revalidate, push. This run hit exactly that: 1c2377e -> e6f5486 (a fast-forward race, ancestor confirmed), rebased, all gates re-run, pushed 353ef6d.

Run IDs collide across concurrent runs: this run was assigned NEX-2026-11-27-61, which an earlier run had already used in EXECUTION_LOG.md. The entry was renumbered to NEX-2026-11-27-66 to match its task ID. Check the log before writing a run ID.

The heredoc in this environment echoes its own body and can corrupt multi-KB writes. This run hit it twice (log append and checkpoint). Every multi-line write must go through `file_editor` to a file and then run the file. The corruption is in the input path: verify the target file afterwards (byte/line count vs the committed blob).
NEX-063's two-signature floor for `high` risk has no production caller: `org_search` is also non-delegable, so no agent token reaches it. Tested as a pure function.
Risk tiering covers only the capability, not request-level signals (bulk volume, unusual patterns, export size). Deferred with reasons in ADR-016.
Approval `preview` is not implemented - no proposal surface exists to render.
The rate-limit obligation is a per-process bound with the in-memory adapter.
Thirteen slices now stack in PR #5. Review cost is real.

An approval records the threshold in force when it was opened. Any future control that tightens a threshold between open and spend must remember that `is_usable` cannot detect the gap - NEX-068 fixed the one place that mattered, not the pattern.

The approval record is additive and nullable: pre-existing policy_versions rows keep approved_at/approved_by NULL while being in force. The domain refuses to *construct* such a version, so only legacy rows are affected - but any consumer that assumes 'in force implies approved' must handle NULL.

Run IDs are assigned independently of the log and have collided twice now (NEX-2026-11-27-61 reused, and NEX-069 written as NEX-066 in its commit message). Grep EXECUTION_LOG.md and CHECKPOINT.json for the next free ID BEFORE writing the commit message.

A legacy policy version in force carries no approval record. has_approval_record() is the only correct way to ask; any new consumer that reads `status == 'published'` as 'a human approved this' reintroduces the ambiguity NEX-069 documents rather than removes.

decisions_this_run: D-070e: tolerate a legacy in-force policy version with NULL approval columns rather than backfill. Backfilling invents an approver; the column exists so the audit trail cannot do that.
D-070f: still reject a half-written approval (exactly one of the two columns set). No legitimate writer produces that state, so accepting it would only hide a bug.
D-070g: has_approval_record() is a separate question from status, because `published` no longer implies `reviewed` for legacy rows. RollbackPolicy asks the former.
D-070h: RollbackPolicy refuses to restore a legacy version's rules instead of inheriting an approval that does not exist, and says so in the error message with the remediation.
run_summary: NEX-065 verified against CI (4/4 at 2d59c74) and re-validated locally at 1472 passed. While doing so, found and fixed a defect that made NEX-065's own migration unupgradable on any database that had already published a policy: a table-wide CHECK constraint required an approver on rows written before the column existed. The test that should have caught it was itself broken and had been vacuous. Both fixed; five tests were proved to fail with the fix reverted. Recorded as NEX-069 because the commit message says NEX-066, an ID already in use.
head_drift_policy: `commit` names the last head whose *product* code was verified by CI, not necessarily the branch tip. NEXUS checkpoint updates are themselves docs-only commits, so the tip advances one commit past `commit` every time this file is written - chasing it is an unbounded loop (run 64 hit this: 7456a89 -> 974d03f -> c49befe, each fix creating a new tip). On reconciliation, compare the product tree, not the SHA: `git diff <commit>..HEAD -- src/ tests/` being empty means `commit` is still an accurate description of what CI verified.
commit_note: A checkpoint commit cannot name itself. 787ed57 is the last substantive commit; every later commit on this branch is a docs-only checkpoint that descends from it, so its CI still compiles and tests the same product code. To find the live head, poll `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/agentic-enterprise-platform` rather than trusting this field. Each such docs commit also cancels the previous head's in-flight CI (branch concurrency), so `conclusion: cancelled` means superseded, never failed.
